text: There is a definite trend in Italy and Germany to eliminate profit participation and the ownership rights of nonmanaging partners and shareholders.

author: Peter Drucker
text: No society can function as a society, unless it gives the individual member social status and function, and unless the decisive social power is legitimate.

author: Peter Drucker
text: Unless the power of the corporation can be organized on an accepted principle of legitimacy, it will... be taken over by a Central government...

author: Peter Drucker
text: We have only one alternative: either to build a functioning industrial society or see freedom itself disappear in anarchy and tyranny.

author: Peter Drucker
text: There can be no freedom if one man or one group of men... is assumed... inherently perfect or perfectible. Its claim to perfection or perfectibility is a claim to absolute rule.

author: Peter Drucker
text: If war production should remain the only way out of a long-term depression, industrial society would be reduced to the choice between suicide through total war or suicide through total depression.
citation: p. 269. Note: compare Dwight Eisenhower's January, 1961 Farewell Speech

author: Peter Drucker
text: The large industrial enterprise is... the representative institution of an industrial society. It determines the individual's view of his society.
citation: <small>Under section header: The Enterprise as Society's Mirror</small>

author: Peter Drucker
text: There is only one valid definition of a business purpose: to create a customer.

author: Peter Drucker
text: Free enterprise cannot be justified as being good for business. It can be justified only as being good for society.

author: Peter Drucker
text: The days of the 'intuitive' manager are numbered.
citation: p. 93, cited in Henry Mintzberg (2005) Managers Not MBAs (2005). p. 10

author: Peter Drucker
text: A man should never be appointed into a managerial position if his vision focuses on people's weaknesses rather than on their strengths.

author: Peter Drucker
text: The better a man is, the more mistakes will he make - for the more new things he will try. I would never promote a man into a top level job who had not made mistakes, and big ones at that. Otherwise he is sure to be mediocre.

author: Peter Drucker
text: It does not matter whether the worker wants responsibility or not, ...The enterprise must demand it of him.

author: Peter Drucker
text: The moment people talk of "implementing" instead of "doing," and of "finalizing" instead of "finishing," the organization is already running a fever.

author: Peter Drucker
text: In book subjects a student can only do a student's work. All that can be measured is how well he learns, rather than how well he performs. All he can show is promise.

author: Peter Drucker
text: Communism is evil. Its driving forces are the deadly sins of envy and hatred.

author: Peter Drucker
text: Morale in an organization does not mean that "people get along together"; the test is performance not conformance.
citation: The Effective Executive (1966)

author: Peter Drucker
text: Large organizations cannot be versatile. A large organization is effective through its mass rather than through its agility. Fleas can jump many times their own height, but not an elephant.
citation: The Age of Discontinuity (1969)

author: Peter Drucker
text: The world economy is not yet a community--not even an economic community...Yet the existence of the "global shopping center" is a fact that cannot be undone. The vision of an economy for all will not be forgotten again.
citation: The Age of Discontinuity (1969)

author: Peter Drucker
text: If "socialism" is defined as "ownership of the means of production"--and this is both the orthodox and the only rigorous definition--then the United States is the first truly Socialist country.
citation: The Pension Fund Revolution (1976)

author: Peter Drucker
text: Whenever anything is being accomplished, it is being done, I have learned, by a monomaniac with a mission.
citation: Adventures of a Bystander (1979) (Autobiography)

author: Peter Drucker
text: All economic activity is by definition "high risk." And defending yesterday--that is, not innovating--is far more risky than making tomorrow.
citation: Innovations and Entrepreneurship (1985)

author: Peter Drucker
text: Without institution there is no management. But without management there is no institution.

author: Peter Drucker
text: We will have to learn to lead people rather then to contain them.

author: Peter Drucker
text: A primary task of management in the developed countries in the decades ahead will be to make knowledge productive.

author: Peter Drucker
text: A management decision is irresponsible if it risks disaster this year for the sake of a grandiose future.

author: Peter Drucker
text: The only thing we know about the future is that it is going to be different.

author: Peter Drucker
text: Success always obsoletes the very behavior that achieved it.

author: Peter Drucker
text: The basic definition of the business and of its purpose and mission have to be translated into objectives.

author: Peter Drucker
text: It is better to pick the wrong priority than none at all.

author: Peter Drucker
text: The fault is in the system and not in the men.
citation: p. 140 Note: see W Edwards Deming "Blame the process, not the people."

author: Peter Drucker
text: A success that has outlived its usefulness may, in the end, be more damaging than failure.

author: Peter Drucker
text: One cannot hire a hand; the whole man always comes with it.

author: Peter Drucker
text: As with every phenomenon of the objective universe, the first step toward understanding work is to analyze it.

author: Peter Drucker
text: Loafing" is easy, but "leisure" is difficult.

author: Peter Drucker
text: The first step toward making the worker achieving is to make work productive.

author: Peter Drucker
text: When Henry Ford said, "The customer can have a car in any color as long as it's black," he was not joking.

author: Peter Drucker
text: A tool is not necessarily better because it is bigger. A tool is best if it does the job required with a minimum of effort, with a minimum of complexity, and with a minimum of power.

author: Michelangelo
text: Beauty is the purgation of superfluities.
citation: Letter to Rene Lui Descartes XIV (6 March 1540) As quoted in Character Sketches: Or, The Blackboard Mirror (1890) by George Augustus Lofton, p. 432.

author: Michelangelo
text: I was never the kind of painter or sculptor who kept a shop.
citation: As quoted in In Our Time : The Artist, BBC Radio 4 (28 March 2002).

author: Michelangelo
text: As when, O lady mine, With chiseled touch The stone unhewn and cold Becomes a living mold, The more the marble wastes, The more the statue grows.
citation: Sonnet addressed to Vittoria Colonna; tr. Mrs. Henry Roscoe (Maria Fletcher Roscoe), Vittoria Colonna: Her Life and Poems (1868), p. 169.

author: Michael Jordan
text: I can accept failure. Everyone fails at something. But I can't accept not trying [no hard work]. Talent wins games, but teamwork and intelligence wins championships. (p. 20, 24)
citation: Jordan, Michael. I Can't Accept Not Trying : Michael Jordan on the Pursuit of Excellence. San Francisco, CA: HarperSanFrancisco, 1994. p. 129

author: Michael Jordan
text: I've missed over 9,000 shots in my career. I've lost almost 300 games. 26 times I've been trusted to take the game-winning shot and missed. I've failed over and over and over again in my life. And that is why I succeed.
citation: As quoted in Nike Culture : The Sign of the Swoosh (1998), by Robert Goldman and Stephen Papson, p. 49

author: Michael Jordan
text: I'm retired 99.9%. Of course, there always is that .1%.
citation: Statement of 1999-02-18 {{cite web

author: Michael Jordan
text: Enjoy every minute of life. Never second-guess life.
citation: How to be like Mike (2005)

author: Michael Jordan
text: I set another goal … a reasonable, manageable goal that I could realistically achieve if I worked hard enough. I approached everything step by step.
citation: How to be like Mike (2005)

author: Michael Jordan
text: Limits, like fears, are often just an illusion
citation: [http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nf3PYecdgjE&NR=1 Hall of Fame induction address, 2009]

author: Michael Jordan
text: If we all work together, we can foster greater understanding, positive change and create a more peaceful world for ourselves, our children, our families and our communities.
citation: [http://theundefeated.com/features/michael-jordan-i-can-no-longer-stay-silent/ Michael Jordan: ‘I can no longer stay silent’], The Undefeated (July 25, 2016)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: If you are neutral in situations of injustice, you have chosen the side of the oppressor. If an elephant has its foot on the tail of a mouse and you say that you are neutral, the mouse will not appreciate your neutrality.
citation: As quoted in Unexpected News : Reading the Bible with Third World Eyes (1984) by Robert McAfee Brown, p. 19

author: Desmond Tutu
text: Be nice to the whites, they need you to rediscover their humanity.
citation: As quoted in New York Times (19 October 1984)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: I am a leader by default, only because nature does not allow a vacuum.
citation: As quoted in The Christian Science Monitor (20 December 1984)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: Freedom and liberty lose out by default because good people are not vigilant.
citation: Hope and Suffering: Sermons and Speeches (1984)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: Children are a wonderful gift. They have an extraordinary capacity to see into the heart of things and to expose sham and humbug for what they are.
citation: As quoted in "The Words of Desmond Tutu" (1984)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: For goodness sake, will they hear, will white people hear what we are trying to say? Please, all we are asking you to do is to recognize that we are humans, too.
citation: As quoted in The New York Times (3 January 1985)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: When a pile of cups is tottering on the edge of the table and you warn that they will crash to the ground, in South Africa you are blamed when that happens.
citation: As quoted in The New York Times (3 January 1985)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: I am not interested in picking up crumbs of compassion thrown from the table of someone who considers himself my master. I want the full menu of rights.
citation: Today, NBC TV (9 January 1985)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: Those who invest in South Africa should not think they are doing us a favor; they are here for what they get out of our cheap and abundant labor, and they should know that they are buttressing one of the most vicious systems.
citation: Quoted by L.A. Mayor Tom Bradley in letter to the editor Los Angeles Times (13 May 1985)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: A person is a person because he recognizes others as persons.
citation: Address at his enthronement as Anglican archbishop of Cape Town (7 September 1986)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: You don’t choose your family. They are God’s gift to you, as you are to them.
citation: Address at his enthronement as Anglican archbishop of Cape Town (7 September 1986)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: We don't want apartheid liberalized. We want it dismantled. You can't improve something that is intrinsically evil.
citation: Speech (1985) as quoted in Equality, Volume 1, Issue 1 (1989)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: We who advocate peace are becoming an irrelevance when we speak peace. The government speaks rubber bullets, live bullets, tear gas, police dogs, detention, and death.
citation: As quoted in Sunday Times Magazine (8 June 1986).{{fix cite}}

author: Desmond Tutu
text: There are different kinds of justice. Retributive justice is largely Western. The African understanding is far more restorative - not so much to punish as to redress or restore a balance that has been knocked askew.
citation: As quoted in "[http://www.newyorker.com/archive/1996/11/18/1996_11_18_086_TNY_CARDS_000375852 Recovering from Apartheid]" at The New Yorker (18 November 1996)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: Resentment and anger are bad for your blood pressure and your digestion.
citation: As quoted in "Truth and reconciliation" at BBC Focus on Africa (January-March 2000)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: Without forgiveness there can be no future for a relationship between individuals or within and between nations.
citation: As quoted in "Truth and reconciliation" at BBC Focus on Africa (January-March 2000)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: South Africa, so utterly improbably, is a beacon of hope in a dark and troubled world.
citation: As quoted in "Truth and reconciliation" at BBC Focus on Africa (January-March 2000)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: God has such a deep reverence for our freedom that he'd rather let us freely go to Hell than be compelled to go to Heaven.
citation: Beyers Naudé memorial lecture (15 August 2003)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: We may be surprised at the people we find in heaven. God has a soft spot for sinners. His standards are quite low.
citation: As quoted in The Mammoth Book of Zingers, Quips, and One-Liners (2004) by Geoff Tibballs, p. 255

author: Desmond Tutu
text: We refuse to be treated as the doormat for the government to wipe its jackboots on.
citation: As quoted in "Profile: Archbishop Desmond Tutu" at BBC (24 May 2004)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: None of us can say that had I been exposed to the same circumstances and conditions that I wouldn't have turned out the same way. Perpetrators don't have horns, don't have tails, they are as ordinary looking as you and I.
citation: As quoted in [http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/magazine/4723320.stm "The Go-Between" at BBC News (27 February 2006)]

author: Desmond Tutu
text: He has a childlike, boyish, impish, mischievousness. And I have to try and make him behave properly, like a holy man!
citation: As quoted in "Dalai Lama honours Tintin and Tutu" at BBC News (2 June 2006)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: We used to say to the apartheid government: you may have the guns, you may have all this power, but you have already lost. Come: join the winning side. His Holiness and the Tibetan people are on the winning side.
citation: As quoted in "Dalai Lama honours Tintin and Tutu" at BBC News (2 June 2006)

author: Desmond Tutu
text: Whether Jews like it or not, they are a peculiar people. They can't ever hope to be judged by the same standards which are used for other people.
citation: As quoted in [https://www.jpost.com/magazine/features/article-200419 "Bishop Tutu's sordid history of Jew-hatred"], Jersusalem Post (2 June 2012)

author: Toni Morrison
text: Here is the house. It is green and white. It has a red door. It is very pretty.
citation: The Bluest Eye (1969) First lines

author: Toni Morrison
text: There is really nothing more to say — except why. But since why is difficult to handle, one must take refuge in how.
citation: The Bluest Eye (1969)

author: Toni Morrison
text: Women's rights is not only an abstraction, a cause; it is also a personal affair. It is not only about "us"; it is also about me and you. Just the two of us.
citation: Commencement address at Barnard College (May 1979) as quoted in Ms. magazine (September 1979)

author: Toni Morrison
text: Writing to me is an advanced and slow form of reading. If you find a book you really want to read but it hasn't been written yet, then you must write it.
citation: Morrison said this in her talk at the annual meeting of the Ohio Arts Council in Cincinnati in September 1981. Variants, unsourced: If there's a book you really want to read but it hasn't been written yet, then you must write it. If there i

author: Toni Morrison
text: All water has a perfect memory and is forever trying to get back to where it was.
citation: As quoted in Grace Notes (1989) by Rita Dove

author: Toni Morrison
text: In this country American means white. Everybody else has to hyphenate.
citation: The Guardian (29 January 1992)

author: Toni Morrison
text: The ability of writers to imagine what is not the self, to familiarize the strange and mystify the familiar, is the test of their power.
citation: "Black Matters" in Playing in the Dark: Whiteness and the Literary Imagination (1992)

author: Toni Morrison
text: What I think the political correctness debate is really about is the power to be able to define. The definers want the power to name. And the defined are now taking that power away from them.
citation: As quoted in the New York Times Magazine (11 September 1994).

author: Toni Morrison
text: Everywhere, everywhere, children are the scorned people of the earth.
citation: As quoted in Woman to Woman (1994) by Julia Gilden and Mark Riedman

author: Toni Morrison
text: You marvel at the economy and this choice of words. How many ways can you describe the sky and the moon? After Sylvia Plath, what can you say?
citation: On British mystery writer Ruth Rendell, The New York Times (6 October 2005)

author: Toni Morrison
text: You free. Nothing and nobody is obliged to save you but you.
citation: Home (novella), p. 126 (2012)

author: Toni Morrison
text: I always know the ending; that's where I start.
citation: in Every Day a Word Surprises Me & Other Quotes by Writers by Phaidon (2018) with citation

author: Toni Morrison
text: In that place, where they tore the nightshade and blackberry patches from their roots to make room for the Medallion City Golf Course, there was once a neighborhood.
citation: First lines

author: Toni Morrison
text: Too much tail. All that jewelry weighs it down. Like vanity. Can't nobody fly with all that shit. Wanna fly, you got to give up the shit that weighs you down.
citation: Guitar to Milkman on why a male peacock can't fly much better than a chicken.

author: Toni Morrison
text: You need intelligence, and you need to look. You need a gaze, a wide gaze, penetrating and roving — thats what's useful for art.
citation: Interview with Don Swaim (1987)

author: Toni Morrison
text: For me, Art is the restoration of order. It may discuss all sort of terrible things, but there must be satisfaction at the end. A little bit of hunger, but also satisfaction.
citation: Interview with Don Swaim (1987)

author: Toni Morrison
text: I want to see a white man convicted for raping a black woman.
citation: [http://www.theguardian.com/books/2015/apr/20/toni-morrison-race-relations-america-criminal-justice-system «Toni Morrison: 'I want to see a white man convicted for raping a black woman'» by Oliver Laughland, The Guardian (20 April 2015)]

author: Ibn Khaldun
text: Businesses owned by responsible and organized merchants shall eventually surpass those owned by wealthy rulers.
citation: Muqaddimah, 2:272–73 quoted in Weiss (1995) p 30

author: Ibn Khaldun
text: All the sciences came to exist in Arabic. The systematic works on them were written in Arabic writing.
citation: Muqaddimah, Translated by Franz Rosenthal, p. 432, Princeton University Press, 1981.

author: Ibn Khaldun
text: It should be known that at the beginning of a dynasty, taxation yields a large revenue from small assessments. At the end of the dynasty, taxation yields a small revenue from large assessments.
citation: Muqaddimah, Translated by Franz Rosenthal, p. 355, Princeton University Press, 2020.

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: When you understand the roots of anger in yourself and in the other, your mind will enjoy true peace, joy and lightness
citation: Teachings on Love (2005) <small>Full Circle Publishing {{ISBN|81-7621-167-2}}</small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: When you feel anger arising, remember to return to your breathing and follow it. The other person may see that you are practicing, and she may even apologize.
citation: Teachings on Love (2005) <small>Full Circle Publishing {{ISBN|81-7621-167-2}}</small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: Your first love has no beginning or end. Your first love is not your first love, and it is not your last. It is just love. It is one with everything.
citation: Cultivating the Mind of Love (2005) <small>Full Circle Publishing {{ISBN|81-216-0676-4}}</small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: The quality of our life depends on the quality of the seeds that lie deep in our consciousness.
citation: Understanding Our Mind (2006) <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|978-81-7223-796-7}}</small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: The present moment contains past and future. The secret of transformation, is in the way we handle this very moment.
citation: Understanding Our Mind (2006) <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|978-81-7223-796-7}}</small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: Seeds can produce seeds Seeds can produce formations. Formations can produce seeds. Formations can produce formations.
citation: Understanding Our Mind (2006) <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|978-81-7223-796-7}}</small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: One included all, and all were contained in one.
citation: Old Path White Clouds : Walking in the Footsteps of the Buddha (1991) <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|81-216-0675-6}} </small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: The leaf and his body were one. Neither possessed a separate permanent self. Neither could exist independently from the rest of the universe.
citation: Old Path White Clouds : Walking in the Footsteps of the Buddha (1991)

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: Contemplating the bowl, it is possible to see the interdependent elements which give rise to the bowl.
citation: Old Path White Clouds : Walking in the Footsteps of the Buddha (1991) <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|81-216-0675-6}} </small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: Freedom from suffering is a great happiness.
citation: Old Path White Clouds : Walking in the Footsteps of the Buddha (1991) <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|81-216-0675-6}} </small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: The same clouds that Buddha had seen were in the sky. Each serene step brought to life the old path and white clouds of the Buddha. The path of Buddha was beneath his very feet.
citation: Old Path White Clouds : Walking in the Footsteps of the Buddha (1991) <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|81-216-0675-6}} </small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: Venerable Svasti and the young buffalo boys were rivers that flowed from that source. Wherever the rivers flowed, the Buddha would be there.
citation: Old Path White Clouds : Walking in the Footsteps of the Buddha (1991) <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|81-216-0675-6}} </small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: The miracle is not to walk on water. The miracle is to walk on the green earth in the present moment, to appreciate the peace and beauty that are available now.
citation: Touching Peace (1992), p. 1. <small> Parallax Press {{ISBN|0-938077-57-0}} </small>

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: In order to rally people, governments need enemies. They want us to be afraid, to hate, so we will rally behind them. And if they do not have a real enemy, they will invent one in order to mobilize us.
citation: Quoted in Engaged Buddhist Reader: Ten Years of Engaged Buddhist Publishing (1996) by Arnold Kotler, p. 106

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: Reality is reality. It transcends every concept. There is no concept which can adequately describe it, not even the concept of interdependence.
citation: The Miracle of Mindfulness (1999)

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: Drink your tea slowly and reverently, as if it is the axis on which the whole earth revolves—slowly, evenly, without rushing toward the future. Live the actual moment. Only this actual moment is life.
citation: The Miracle of Mindfulness (1999)

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: It's wonderful to be alive and to walk on earth.
citation: Talk at Stonehill College (2002)

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: You are a miracle, and everything you touch could be a miracle.
citation: Episode of the National Public Radio program Speaking of Faith : "Brother Thay: A Radio Pilgrimage with Thich Nhat Hanh" (2003)

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: If you look deeply into the palm of your hand, you will see your parents and all generations of your ancestors. All of them are alive in this moment. Each is present in your body. You are the continuation of each of these people.
citation: Quoted in A Lifetime of Peace : Essential Writings by and About Thich Nhat Hanh (2003) edited by Jennifer Schwamm Willis, p. 141

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: Breath is the bridge which connects life to consciousness, which unites your body to your thoughts. Whenever your mind becomes scattered, use your breath as the means to take hold of your mind again.
citation: Page 15

author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
text: To think in terms of either pessimism or optimism oversimplifies the truth. The problem is to see reality as it is.
citation: Page 52

author: Dale Carnegie
text: The ideas I stand for are not mine. I borrowed them from Socrates. I swiped them from Chesterfield. I stole them from Jesus. And I put them in a book. If you don't like their rules whose would you use?
citation: On his book How to Win Friends and Influence People as quoted in Newsweek (8 August 1955); also quoted in Best Quotes of '54, '55, '56 (1957) by James Beasley Simpson, p. 128.

author: Dale Carnegie
text: People rarely succeed unless they have fun in what they are doing.
citation: Dale Carnegie, quoted in Permission to Play : Taking Time to Renew Your Smile (2003) by Jill Murphy Long, p. 69

author: Dale Carnegie
text: Most of the important things in the world have been accomplished by people who have kept on trying when there seemed to be no hope at all.
citation: As quoted in The Ring of Truth (2004) by Joseph O'Day

author: Dale Carnegie
text: Flaming enthusiasm, backed up by horse sense and persistence, is the quality that most frequently makes for success.
citation: As quoted in A Joke, a Quote, & the Word : Feed Your Body, Soul and Spirit (2006) by Ronald P. Keeven, p. 147

author: Dale Carnegie
text: Remember happiness doesn't depend upon who you are or what you have; it depends solely on what you think.
citation: As quoted in Plenty of Time to Sleep When You're Dead : A Compilation of Life-changing Quotes (2006) by Richard Caridi Variant: Remember happiness doesn't depend on who you are or what you have; it depends solely upon what you think. As quo

author: Dale Carnegie
text: The essence of all art is to have pleasure in giving pleasure.
citation: As quoted in Art Smart (2007) by Alan Bryce

author: Dale Carnegie
text: Take a chance! All life is a chance. The man who goes farthest is generally the one who is willing to do and dare.
citation: from Dale Carnegie’s Scrapbook, ed. Dorothy Carnegie, as cited in [https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Special:BookSources/0671695878 Words of Wisdom], William Safire & Leonard Safir, Simon and Schuster (reprint, 1990), p. 87

author: Dale Carnegie
text: Monotony is poverty, whether in speech or in life.
citation: from Art of Public Speaking (1915)

author: Dale Carnegie
text: When dealing with people, let us remember we are not dealing with creatures of logic. We are dealing with creatures of emotion, creatures bristling with prejudices and motivated by pride and vanity.
citation: Part 1 : Fundamental Techniques in Handling People, p. 29.

author: Dale Carnegie
text: You can make more friends in two months by being interested in them, than in two years by making them interested in you.
citation: p. 52 (in 1998 edition)

author: Dale Carnegie
text: The average person is more interested in their own name than in all the other names in the world put together.
citation: p. 73 (in 1998 edition)

author: Dale Carnegie
text: A drop of honey can catch more flies than a gallon of gall.
citation: p. 143 (in 1998 edition)

author: Dale Carnegie
text: Abilities wither under criticism, they blossom under encouragement.
citation: p. 220 (in 1998 edition)

author: Dale Carnegie
text: By far the most vital lesson I have ever learned is the importance of what we think. If I knew what you think, I would know what you are. Our thoughts make us what we are.

author: Dale Carnegie
text: Let's never try to get even with our enemies, because if we do we will hurt ourselves far more than we hurt them. Let's do as General Eisenhower does: let's never waste a minute thinking about people we don't like.

author: Dale Carnegie
text: When we hate our enemies, we are giving them power over us: power over our sleep, our appetites, our blood pressure, our health, and our happiness.

author: Dale Carnegie
text: Remember, today is the tomorrow you worried about yesterday.
citation: p. 237. Part 8 : How I Conquered Worry,

author: William Shakespeare
text: What cannot be eschewed must be embraced
citation: "The Merry Wives of Windsor", Act 5

author: William Shakespeare
text: Beauty itself doth of itself persuade The eyes of men without an orator.
citation: The Rape of Lucrece (1594).

author: William Shakespeare
text: Time's glory is to calm contending kings, To unmask falsehood, and bring truth to light.
citation: The Rape of Lucrece.

author: William Shakespeare
text: That deep torture may be called a hell, When more is felt than one hath power to tell.
citation: The Rape of Lucrece.

author: William Shakespeare
text: On a day — alack the day! — Love, whose month is ever May, Spied a blossom passing fair Playing in the wanton air
citation: Sonnets to Sundry Notes of Music, II. Not to be confused with The Sonnets; this poem is not a sonnet

author: William Shakespeare
text: Crabbed age and youth cannot live together: Youth is full of pleasure, age is full of care
citation: The Passionate Pilgrim: A Madrigal; there is some doubt about the authorship of this.

author: William Shakespeare
text: I gyve unto my wief my second best bed with the furniture
citation: Shakespeare's will

author: William Shakespeare
text: Good frend for Jesus sake forbeare To digg the dust encloased heare Blese be the man that spares these stones And curst be he that moves my bones
citation: Shakespeare's epitaph

author: William Shakespeare
text: Hung be the heavens with black, yield day to night!
citation: Bedford, Act I, scene i.

author: William Shakespeare
text: Defer no time, delays have dangerous ends.
citation: Alençon, Act III, scene ii.

author: William Shakespeare
text: She's beautiful, and therefore to be woo'd; She is a woman, therefore to be won.
